title: The Alchemy Project
headline: Many capabilities. One considered architecture.
intro: Alchemy is the work behind Rasen Falcon: semantic objects, distributed services and portable applications joined without erasing their independent authority.
summary: A project in applied systems architecture, where ooRexx, native runtimes, service contracts and the MI/MU mesh can work together without making any one transport compulsory.

sections.heading: The object is the centre
sections.body: Alchemy treats an object as more than a bag of fields. Identity, method authority, evidence and protected behaviour matter. ooRexx is a principal language of application behaviour and orchestration, while native and cross-language components contribute specialised capabilities.

sections.heading: Connect, without compulsory coupling
sections.body: Local direct invocation, standalone JSON-RPC and Queue Fabric are different means of reaching a service. Queue Fabric is valuable for durable jobs, retained status and scheduling, but an ordinary service should not be forced to depend on it when simpler interaction is sufficient.

sections.heading: A distributed system that can explain itself
sections.body: The RexxOS MI/MU mesh, compute placement, job migration and storage services are designed to carry work and evidence between machines. The aim is reliable continuation, not a claim that every workstream has reached production qualification.
